question: In a new game the order-of-battle files give carriers air groups with no name; the start save has them as `1st Air wing` and their wings as `1st CAG`. Which function names them and when, from which text, by what count, and does it hold for every case in Germany1936_01_01_00.hoi3?

addresses.name: CInGameIdler_Enter_NameUnnamedUnit
addresses.no_signature: An address inside CInGameIdler::Enter (0x25A2B0): the new-game arm of the per-unit walk.
addresses.comment: **Where every unit a new game's order of battle left without a name gets one - a carrier's air group among them.** In CInGameIdler::Enter's walk over each country's units (+0xBAC, from the head, 0x65B7F0), on the arm taken only where loaded_from_save (+0xD9C) is clear (`je 0x65b8f2` at 0x65B8BE): the unit's name through CUnit slot 7 (GetName) into a temporary; **only where its length (+0x10) is exactly 0** (`sete` at 0x65B907) CUnit_MakeName(unit@EAX, out@ESI, country, province 0) at 0x65B95F - CCountry::MakeUnitName for the unit's first brigade's definition and its oob_level - and CUnit_SetName (0x65B970), which registers the name in the country's set of names in use (CCountry +0x84). Then, for both kinds of game, the starting experience of each brigade (0x65B9B8, FINDINGS-unitstart.md section 6). So an unnamed unit is named after the country's whole order of battle has been read (LoadOobFile, 0x65B4EC, earlier in the same per-country pass) and in the order of the country's unit list, which for the air groups aboard carriers is the order of their `air` blocks in the file (CShip_LoadKey_Air appends each as its block closes). An air unit is oob_level 6, so its name is AIR_NAME with the first number whose text the country has not used - `1st Air wing`, `2nd Air wing` in English. A loaded game never takes this arm, and load_oob (CLoadOOBEffect::Execute, 0x5BBD00) reaches none of the naming functions, so a nameless air group loaded by that effect in a running game stays nameless (likely). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitstart.md, section 6a.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x65B4C0-0x65BAFE (VAs): the +0xD9C test at 0x65B8B7 branching to 0x65B8F2; `mov edx,[eax+0x1c]; call edx` (CUnit slot 7 is GetName in project.json's vftable_slots); `cmp dword ptr [eax+0x10],0; sete`; `je 0x65b9b8` skipping the naming when non-empty; `call 0x4cb580` (CUnit_MakeName) with `push 0; push country` and `mov eax,edi` (the unit); `call 0x5c48e0` (CUnit_SetName). findRefs --callers 0x4CB580 lists this as the only call inside CInGameIdler::Enter. Checked against the start save: all 24 carrier groups of ENG, USA, JAP and FRA carry `Nth Air wing` with N the position of their `air` block in the country's 1936 file, Hermes' 9th although the save writes it 4th. Wrong if a nameless unit's name came from somewhere earlier - but CUnit_MakeName has no caller on the load path (11 callers, none in CUnit::LoadKey, CShip::LoadKey or CCountry::AfterLoad).

addresses.name: CUnit_LoadKey_Wing
addresses.no_signature: An address inside CUnit::LoadKey (0x1B6E90): its `wing` case.
addresses.comment: **CUnit::LoadKey's `wing` case, and where a wing the file leaves unnamed is named - as it is read.** A CWing (0xD8 bytes: CSubUnit::CSubUnit, vftable 0x15BDDC4); its owner (+0x94/+0x98) copied from the unit's (CUnit +0x124/+0x128) and its unit (+0xB0) set **before** its block is read (its slot 3, Load); AddRegimentToUnit; then its name through CSubUnit slot 8 into a temporary, and **only where that is empty** (0x5B7A00-0x5B7A1A) CCountry::MakeSubUnitName(the owner's country, out, the wing's definition +0x58, home 0, nameSet 0) at 0x5B7A50 and CSubUnit_SetName (0x5B7A63), which registers it in the country's names in use. A wing is not land, so the country's `unit_names` list for its type is tried first; with none (no Their Finest Hour country has a `cag` list) it is SUBUNIT_NAME with the first free number and TYPE the text of `<type>_short` - `1st CAG`. **The wing case never tests the unit's reserve flag**, unlike `regiment` (FINDINGS-unitstart.md section 2). So a carrier group's wing is named during the order of battle's read, in file order, and the group around it later, in CInGameIdler::Enter (CInGameIdler_Enter_NameUnnamedUnit): two separate first-free searches over two different texts that give the same number only because each group holds one wing and both run in file order. The `ship` case at 0x5B7523 has the same shape (a CShip of 0xF8 bytes, +0xB0 set before Load, named by MakeSubUnitName at 0x5B75F0 where empty). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitstart.md, section 6a.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x5B797E-0x5B7A88 (VAs): `push 0xd8; call new; call 0x5a88f0; mov [esi],0x15bddc4`; owner from [ebx+0x11c]/[ebx+0x120] with ebx the CPersistent half (CUnit+8); `mov [esi+0xb0], edi` (edi = ebx-8) before `call [vft+0xc]`; `call 0x5be640` (AddRegimentToUnit); `call [vft+0x20]`; `cmp [eax+0x10],0; sete`; `je 0x5b7f4e`; `push 0; push 0; push [esi+0x58]; push out; push countries[owner]` then `call 0x4cbfd0` and `call 0x5a8bb0`. FINDINGS-unitstart.md already gave 0x5B797E as the wing case. Checked: every one of the 24 carrier wings in the start save is `Nth CAG`, N its file position in its country. Wrong if CSubUnit slot 8 were not the name - but an empty answer here is what the save shows replaced and a named wing in the files keeps its name (3682 of 3682, FINDINGS-unitstart.md section 9).

addresses.name: CShip_LoadKey_Air
addresses.no_signature: An address inside CShip::LoadKey (0x1ADBF0): its one case, `air` (token 0x440).
addresses.comment: **A carrier's air group as an order of battle or a save makes it - with no name.** CShip::LoadKey's one case: a CAir (0x2F4 bytes, constructor 0x5D0460, which sets oob_level 6). Where the ship has its unit (+0xB0, which CUnit::LoadKey's `ship` case sets before the ship's block is read): the air unit is given the unit's idler (slot 28 with CUnit +0x160), the ship's owner (CUnit_SetOwner with +0x94/+0x98), hung under the fleet (CUnit_AttachToParent), based on the carrier (CUnit::SetBase with the ship's base object +0xD8), its block read (its CPersistent half's Load), and **appended to its country's units** (CCountry::AddUnit, 0x5ADCE8) - so the air groups of a country's carriers join its unit list in the order their `air` blocks close, which is file order. Nothing names it here: a block with no `name` leaves it empty until CInGameIdler::Enter names it in a new game (CInGameIdler_Enter_NameUnnamedUnit). Where the ship has no unit the air block is read and the air unit deleted (0x5ADD01). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitstart.md, section 6a.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x5ADBF0-0x5ADD2B (VAs): `cmp eax,0x440; je 0x5adc3b`, else CSubUnit::LoadKey; `push 0x2f4; call new; call 0x5d0460`; `mov eax,[ebx+0xb0]; test; je 0x5add01`; `call [vft+0x70]` with [eax+0x160]; `call 0x5bc460`; `call 0x5b9760`; `lea eax,[ebx+0xd8]; push eax; mov edi,esi; call 0x5cdbe0`; `call [vft+0xc]` on esi+8; `call 0x4e06f0` with countries[owner]. 0x5D0460 writes `mov [esi+0x1f4], 6` at 0x5D048E. The save corroborates the order: each wing's id is one below its group's and a carrier's id above its groups' (HMS Furious: wings 453 and 455, groups 454 and 456, ship 457), the order blocks close in. Wrong if CCountry::AddUnit prepended - its record says appended, and the names' order in the save says the walk met the groups in file order.

addresses.name: CCountry::MakeUnitName
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __stdcall CCountry::MakeUnitName(CCountry* country, Hoi3CString* out, CSubUnitDefinition* definition, int level, CMapProvince* province)
addresses.comment: **A name for a new unit of a given level** (0 theatre, 1 army group, 2 army, 3 corps, 4 division, 5 navy, 6 air). **Only for a division (`cmp [ebp+0x14], 4`)** the country's list of names for the definition's type (CCountry +0xCAC, indexed by the definition's index +0x24, 0x10 an entry holding a vector of 0x1C-byte strings) is tried once round from the cursor at +0xCBC, the cursor left past the one taken; a name already in the country's set of names in use (+0x84, StringHashSet_Find 0xA86F70) is passed over. A fleet or an air unit never looks at a list. Then n = 1, 2, 3 ...: the text of THEATRE_NAME, ARMYGROUP_NAME, ARMY_NAME, CORPS_NAME, DIVISION_NAME, NAVY_NAME or AIR_NAME by level (jump table 0x4CBFA8; DIVISION_NAME past 6) with NUM = n, ORDER = the text of TH, ST, ND or RD by `n % 10` from the table `TH ST ND RD TH TH TH TH TH TH` (0x15C0AF4..), 11 to 13 sent to TH, and TYPE = the text of the definition's key + `_short`; a theatre at n = 1 with a province may take NAMED_THEATHRE instead. **The first n whose text is not in the country's set is returned** - there is no counter, and nothing of it is saved. Five stack arguments, `ret 0x14`. Callers: CUnit_MakeName, CMilitaryConstruction::Deliver, CConstructUnitCommand::Execute, CTransferSubUnitCommand::Execute, CUnitSplitCommand_TakeSubUnit. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-builders.md, section 3, and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitstart.md, section 6a.
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the entry 0x4CB5F0 to `ret 0x14` at 0x4CBFA4 (VAs): the level-4 gate at 0x4CB62C; the list walk with `add eax, 0x84; call 0xa86f70`; the suffix pointers 0x15C0AF4/AF8/AFC/B00 reading `TH`, `ST`, `ND`, `RD`; `idiv`-by-10 by `imul 0x66666667` and `lea eax,[esi-0xb]; cmp eax,2; ja` for 11-13; the jump table over level 0-6 pushing the seven keys; `_short` and `TYPE`; the loop end `call 0xa86f70` on [ebp-0x7c] (= country+0x84), `inc [ebp-0x14]` and back to 0x4CB700. The call in CUnit_MakeName pushes province, level (+0x1F4), definition (first brigade +0x58), out, country - five, matching `ret 0x14`. **Revises**: the entry carried no signature and was `inferred`; the comment said the list was tried 'for a division' without saying a fleet or an air unit never is. Wrong if the jump at 0x4CB633 were taken for level 6 - it is `jne` on 4.
addresses.revises: The entry had no signature and was inferred; now read to its end - five stack arguments placed, the list path shown to be a division's only, and the absence of any counter stated.

addresses.name: CCountry::MakeSubUnitName
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __stdcall CCountry::MakeSubUnitName(CCountry* country, Hoi3CString* out, CSubUnitDefinition* definition, CMapProvince* home, void* nameSet)
addresses.comment: **A name for a new brigade, ship or wing.** A type that is not land (is_land, +0x2D, clear) is first tried against the country's list for it (CCountry +0xCAC by the definition's index, from the cursor +0xCBC, once round), passing over a name in the country's set of names in use (+0x84) - as CCountry::MakeUnitName does for a division; a land brigade never is - the lists under brigade types name divisions. Then n = 1, 2, 3 ...: REGIMENT_NAME for a land brigade and SUBUNIT_NAME for the rest, with NUM, ORDER (the same TH ST ND RD table, 11-13 TH) and TYPE (the text of the definition's key + `_short`), and HOME (the home province's name, through its +8 half's slot 7) where `home` is given. **The test of 'free'** is the country's set (+0x84, StringHashSet_Find 0xA86F70) where `nameSet` is null and 0x4BC3B0(nameSet, the name) where it is not (not read; CreateRebelsForFaction and ReleaseProvinces pass one, the order-of-battle wing and ship cases, CConstructUnitCommand::Execute, CCreateHigherCommand::Execute, CCreateNewHQCommand::Execute and CMilitaryConstruction::Deliver pass null). A result equal to REGIMENT_NAME, to the empty key, or to the string `aa` (0x15C0E3C) is returned as it is without the test - the key itself only for REGIMENT_NAME; a missing SUBUNIT_NAME is not caught there (read only as far as the three compares). No counter is kept. Five stack arguments, `ret 0x14`. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-builders.md, section 3, and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitstart.md, section 6a.
addresses.evidence: Decoded from the entry 0x4CBFD0 to `ret 0x14` at 0x4CCCB6 (VAs): `cmp byte ptr [ecx+0x2d], bl; jne 0x4cc0c2` skipping the list for a land type; the list walk with `add eax,0x84; call 0xa86f70`; `cmp byte ptr [eax+0x2d],bl; je 0x4cc715` choosing SUBUNIT_NAME over REGIMENT_NAME; `mov edi,[ebp+0x14]; cmp edi,ebx; je` around HOME; the three string compares at 0x4CCB4E-0x4CCBF8 jumping out to return; `mov esi,[ebp+0x18]; cmp esi,ebx; je 0x4ccc2e` choosing 0x4BC3B0 or the country set; `inc dword ptr [ebp-0x30]; jmp 0x4cc0ca`. Callers' pushes read at 0x485125, 0x545DCC, 0x5DFA3C, 0x5E0F3C, 0x5B7A35 (two zeros) and 0x4BACBD, 0x4C19BC (registers). **Revises**: the entry carried no signature and was `inferred`, and did not know of the fifth argument. Wrong if [ebp+0x18] were not an argument - `ret 0x14` says five dwords.
addresses.revises: The entry had no signature and was inferred; the five stack arguments are placed and the fifth, an alternative names-in-use test, is new.
